summary: Eco-Avatar Activism is a movement, begun in early September 2023, in which environmental activists use computer-generated virtual personas to spread ecological messages and engage audiences. The note describes example avatars, the technology behind them, ethical and psychological concerns about authenticity and overidentification, community events, and measurable influence including a petition with over a million signatures. It closes with the future potential of more immersive, AI-driven advocacy.
one_line: Environmental activists use virtual avatars like Terra Virtua and Marina Blue to boost climate awareness and action, raising ethical questions and driving real-world impact.
key_facts: The Digital Earthrise Movement began on September 5, 2023, with the creation of the avatar Terra Virtua by activist Lila Nguyen.
Terra Virtua was designed with greenery and charm and speaks on climate change, deforestation, and biodiversity loss.
Marina Blue, launched October 20, 2023 by oceanographer and digital artist Hassan Patel, highlights coral reef plight and marine pollution.

On November 17, 2023, Arjun Singh, a software developer and conservationist, released the avatar Forrest Root, which led a VR-based reforestation campaign in which virtual trees planted corresponded to real trees planted around the globe.
Avatar technology ranges from simple 2D animation to complex 3D modeling and motion capture, with machine learning letting avatars answer live questions.
Dr. Emma Richardson of the Environmental Ethical Engagement Institute says the avatars need transparency so users understand they are fabrications for illustrative and educational purposes.
A psychological risk is overidentification with virtual figures, potentially overshadowing real individuals and organizations working on the ground.
The "Green Spirits Gathering," held December 13, 2023, was a virtual roundtable of multiple eco-avatars viewed by thousands online.
Eco-avatars are credited with viral challenges on reducing carbon footprints, zero-waste lifestyles, and sustainable food choices.

On January 25, 2024, a virtual protest led by the avatar Green Pulse produced a petition with over a million signatures demanding stricter regulations on single-use plastics, leading to governmental dialogues on policy reforms.
Avatars reach younger demographics through social media, VR experiences, and interactive games, which are harder to reach with traditional campaigns.
Future possibilities include hyper-realistic simulation experiences that transport people to devastated ecosystems.
